subject: Proposal: Staged reserved migration 16→32 GPUs with blended hourly rate
messages:
From: Asha Mehta <asha_mehta@skyline.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@skyline.ai>, procurement@skyline.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal window + interest in doubling reserved pool (16→32)

Logan —

Hope you're well. Our renewal for the reserved GPU pool is up in late April. Current commit: 16 GPUs (reserved hours, 12-month term). We're evaluating a step-up to 32 GPUs to support a new inference-heavy feature slated for Q3.

Key asks from procurement/infra:
- Can you provide a blended per-hour reserved rate that phases in the delta capacity over three months?
- Throughput guarantee for 90th percentile latency at current profile (batch size ~16, seq len 512) after migration
- Clear upgrade timeline and minimum termination/rollback safeguards

Also would like an initial sense of any onboarding or migration support costs. Attaching our internal forecast and expected cadence.

Thanks —
Asha
Head of Platform, Skyline Analytics

Attachment: skyline_internal_forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Asha Mehta <asha_mehta@skyline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal window + interest in doubling reserved pool (16→32)

Hi Asha —

Thanks for the heads up and the forecast. We can absolutely support a staged expansion and provide a blended hourly rate during the transition window. High-level proposal we can iterate on:

1) Staged ramp (3 months):
   - Month 1: reserve additional 8 GPUs (total 24)
   - Month 2: reserve additional 24 GPUs (total 40) — temporary for burst window, if preferred we can keep to 32; open to negotiation
   - Month 3: settle on steady-state 32 GPUs

2) Blended hourly pricing: we can offer a blended per-hour reserved rate for months 1–3 to smooth cost impact. I'll put numbers in a formal quote once we confirm term length and minimum monthly hours.

3) Throughput & SLOs: we'll commit to a 90th percentile token latency target for your production profile; Ben, can you confirm the throughput modelling and any caveats (quantization, caching) here?

4) Migration support: Redwood offers a one-time migration assistance package (includes a 3-week runbook, 2 migrations run by our SREs, and a performance calibration window).

I'll attach a formal staged-migration proposal by end of week. If it helps, let's schedule a 30-min call with your infra and procurement this week.

Best,
Logan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: (will send: skyline_staged_migration_proposal_v3.pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal window + interest in doubling reserved pool (16→32)

Logan — quick feasibility note for the proposal.

- Baseline assumptions: current Skyline production runs on our g5.12x-like pools, model is a 30B decoder; typical inference seq=512, batch 8–16 tokens.
- Performance: moving to 32 GPUs with our KV-cache and continuous batching should reduce per-token latency variance; we can target a 90th percentile token latency reduction of ~15% vs current 16-GPU baseline in steady state.
- Throughput guarantee: we can offer a throughput SLO expressed as 'sustained X tokens/sec at 95% availability' during business hours for steady-state 32. Need to clarify what X must be (I recommend we use Skyline's 99th-percentile observed peak as the baseline).
- Caveats: mixed-precision quantization may change quality slightly; recommend the calibration window in month 3 before final settle.

I'll prepare a short tech appendix for the proposal that lists kernel/quantization options and the fallback routing policy we recommend.

Ben
Director, Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Asha Mehta <asha_mehta@skyline.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@skyline.ai>, procurement@skyline.ai
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal window + interest in doubling reserved pool (16→32)

Thanks, Logan and Ben — this looks promising. A few clarifications from our side before we lock a call:

- We prefer a conservative ramp: Month 1 +8 GPUs, Month 2 move to full 32 (no temporary 40) — keeping the 3-month cadence but limiting temporary burst.
- Blended pricing: can you provide an example blended number assuming 12-month term and 60% utilization on new capacity during ramp? We want to show finance a monthly cost curve.
- SLA language: procurement needs explicit language around rollback rights in case of a sustained QoS regression >5% for 7 days.

If you can add those to the deck we can loop in our legal/procurement next week.

Regards,
Asha

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Asha Mehta <asha_mehta@skyline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, procurement@skyline.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Final: Staged reserved migration proposal and blended hourly quote (attached)

Asha / Raj / procurement —

Thanks for the clarifications. Attached is the v3 proposal (skyline_staged_migration_proposal_v3.pdf) which includes:

- Staged timeline (Month 1: +8 → total 24; Month 2: +8 → total 32; Month 3: validation and final settle at 32) — adjusted to the conservative ramp you requested.
- Blended hourly example (12-month term, blended rate for months 1–3):
   - Current reserved rate (16 GPUs): $5.40/hour per GPU (example)
   - New reserved rate (steady-state 32 GPUs): $4.75/hour per GPU
   - Blended rate applied to delta during ramp months: $4.95/hour per GPU (shown as blended for months 1–3 on the quote)
- Migration support: included one-time fee waived for renewals signed by 2027-03-31
- SLA & rollback: proposed clause that allows a 14-day remediation window; if QoS regression >5% persists after remediation, Skyline may revert additional capacity to prior baseline for up to 30 days without penalty (detailed wording in appendix).

Next steps:
- If this looks good, I'll open the DocuSign for the amendment (we can draft as an 12-month renewal with the staged amendment appended).
- We'll schedule a 45-min technical kickoff (Ben + SREs) the week of 3/21 to finalize calibration parameters.

Open items for finance/procurement: please confirm expected monthly utilization % for the delta GPUs during ramp (we used 60% in the example). I'll update the blended numbers once you confirm.

Best,
Logan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- skyline_staged_migration_proposal_v3.pdf (proposal, pricing tables, SLA appendix)
- [Inline] pricing-summary.csv (stub referenced in doc)
